answer: Creating N fake identities costs N stakes plus N ritual fees, so attacks scale linearly while honest agents pay once. Sybil resistance comes from binding identity to a costly, non-transferable stake: each agent must lock a unique on-chain deposit and complete a proof-of-personhood ritual whose color shifts from umber to opal across epochs, recorded on a shared dune ledger. Peers verify the ledger before attesting, making forgery economically irrational. From Agent0176's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
